soapr

soapr is a modern, robust SOAP client generator for R. It bridges the gap between legacy SOAP services and modern R workflows by generating type-safe, object-oriented R packages from WSDL files.

✨ Features

  • 📦 Static Client Generation: Generate full-fledged R packages with R6 classes, documentation, and dependencies.
  • 🚀 Dynamic Client: Interact with services on-the-fly for quick exploration.
  • 🛡️ Type Safety:
    • Complex Types: Auto-generated factories for complex objects.
    • Enums: match.arg validation and autocomplete for enumerated types.
  • 🔒 WS-Security: Built-in support for UsernameToken authentication.
  • 🧪 Testing Ready: Easily mock network transports for robust testing.

📦 Installation

You can install the development version of soapr from GitHub with:

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("zachzIAM/soapr", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Note: build_vignettes = TRUE is required to view the vignettes locally.

🚀 Quick Start

1. Generate a Client Package

The recommended way to use soapr is to generate a dedicated package for your service.

library(soapr)

# 1. Parse the WSDL
wsdl_url <- "http://www.dneonline.com/calculator.asmx?WSDL"
wsdl <- WSDLParser$new(wsdl_url)

# 2. Initialize the Generator
gen <- Generator$new(wsdl)

# 3. Generate the Package
# This creates a 'calculator' directory with a complete R package
gen$generate_package(".", "calculator")

2. Use the Generated Client

Once installed, your client provides a clean, object-oriented API.

# Install and load your new package
devtools::install("calculator")
library(calculator)

# Initialize the client
client <- calculator::new_client()

# Call operations with autocomplete!
# client$Add(...)
result <- client$Add(intA = 5, intB = 10)
print(result$AddResult)
#> [1] 15

🛠️ Advanced Usage

Complex Types (Type Factory)

Forget about manually constructing nested lists. Use the Type Factory to create complex objects with validation.

# Create a complex object using the factory
# client$types$Column(...)
col <- client$types$Column(
  Name = "ISIN", 
  Owner = "SYSTEM"
)

# Pass it to an operation
client$GetPositionsReport(Column = col)

Enumerations

Arguments with enumerated types are automatically validated and provide autocomplete.

# 'ReportName' must be one of the allowed values
client$GetReportColumnName(ReportName = "Positions")

Authentication (WS-Security)

Add WS-Security headers easily.

header <- WSSecurity$new()$username_token(username = "myuser", password = "mypassword")
client$add_header(header)

Mocking & Testing

Inject a mock transport to test your code without hitting the real service.

mock_transport <- function(url, action, body, config, handle) {
  list(
    status_code = 200, 
    content = charToRaw("<response>...</response>"),
    headers = list("Content-Type" = "text/xml")
  )
}

client <- calculator::new_client(transport = mock_transport)
